result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly identify the div-based time picker, the colour-only outcome and the aria-label mismatch, and both fix them with native radios and a status live region. A is better on rubric item 5 because it says the labelled party-size select is fine and should be kept, while B never names anything worth keeping. B explains in more detail why the scan missed these problems, but its claim that the scan exempted the light-grey contrast is speculation. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same main problems: the div-based time picker with no keyboard access or semantics, the success or failure shown only by border colour, and the aria-label that doesn't match the visible text. Both give good radio-button and live-region fixes. B is better on rubric item 5 because it says the labelled native select is fine and should be kept, and it ties the missing outcome message to her complaint. A wrongly says Enter on a div never fires onclick, but in browse mode screen readers often send a click.
